evidence.quote: I believe that the current policy stance leaves us well positioned to determine the extent and timing of additional adjustments to our policy rate based on the incoming data
progress on disinflation has stalled over the past year, mainly because of tariffs, and inflation remains somewhat elevated relative to our target.
As a monetary policymaker I confront an outlook where there is downside risk to the labor market and upside risk to inflation.

I see the labor market as roughly in balance and expect the unemployment rate to remain near its current level throughout this year. The risks to my labor market forecast, however, are skewed to the downside.
At least in the short term I expect overall inflation to move higher, reflecting a rise in energy prices stemming from the conflict in the Middle East.

parsed.rationale: The speaker supports holding rates near neutral with data-dependent guidance, balancing stalled disinflation and upside inflation risks against downside labor market risks. The net signal is a wait-and-see hold with a slight hawkish tilt from inflation concern.
